## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kuhakajātaka* (Ja 89) is a short narrative included in the single-verse section (*Ekanipāta*) of the Pali *Jātaka* collection. The text opens with the verse starting *Vācā va kira te āsi* ("How plausible was your speech") [Fausböll 1877]. According to its commentary, the Buddha delivered the discourse while residing at Jetavana with reference to a deceitful monk (*kuhaka*), noting that the fuller circumstances of his knavery would be recounted in the *Uddālajātaka* [Fausböll 1877]. In the story of the past (*atītavatthu*), set during the reign of King Brahmadatta in Bārāṇasī, a deceitful false ascetic with matted hair (*kūṭajaṭilakuhakatāpasa*) lived near a village and engaged in deception [Fausböll 1877]. In the resolution of the tale (*samodhāna*), the Buddha reveals that the deceitful ascetic of the past was the dishonest monk, while the wise man (*paṇḍitapurisa*) who rebuked him was the Bodhisatta [Fausböll 1877].
